newsitem.title: BULGARIA: FOCUS-Bulgaria cenbank retracts FP Bank licence.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Bulgaria cenbank retracts FP Bank licence.

text.p: The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) on Thursday retracted the licence of First Private Bank (FPB), citing its failure to collect loans and service its debts.

"The BNB board decided to retract the licence of First Private Bank after it failed to collect extended credits and repay debts of over 200 billion lev to its major creditors during the (one-year) receivership period," a BNB statement said.
FPB officials were not immediately available for comment.
New sequestrators will be appointed for a three-month period to govern the bank. FPB can appeal against the decision, which is effective immediately.
At end-March, FPB owed over 100 billion levs to the state for repayments to depositors, and over 90 billion levs to the BNB, the statement said.
The bank had a heavily negative capital to risk assets ratio due to a lack of provisions against non-performing loans and its registered capital of 2.0 billion levs has not been fully paid in.
"This has thwarted possibilities for attracting potential investors to increase the bank's capital," the statement said.

Under an agreement with the International Monetary Fund, Bulgarian banks should have a minimum six percent capital to risk assets ratio by the end of this year and eight percent by mid-1998 to comply with international standards.
FPB's financial results were even worse at end-April than in March, the BNB said.
The BNB put FPB, Bulgaria's biggest private bank, in receivership on May 17 last year, dismissed its management and appointed sequestrators to help it collect its loans.
The bank was banned from extending credits, servicing payments or dealing in government securities.
On May 31 the BNB initiated a bankruptcy procedure through the courts, but at the end of last year the Sofia City Court ruled against the claim, saying it was not supported by enough evidence.
The BNB appealed against that ruling and the Supreme Court was expected to consider the BNB appeal next month. -- Sofia Newsroom, 3592 911 88
